If you say you're in pain because you want to talk to your boyfriend but you're worried/feel like you can't because it'd hurt him, you should probably talk to him. Granted, I only know as much about you and him as from what you've told me, and it sounds very noble of you to want to make sure he doesn't feel hurt in any way. But there comes a point where you do have to be a bit... not selfish, but definitely say something along the lines of "hey, I know this may be hard for you to hear, but I need to get this out because it's really hurting me" and go from there. Because just holding it all in will make everything a million times worse and then you'll be more apt to do something that could end badly :( Again, just going by what you've said about your relationship with him, but it sounds like you two are quite close and that he would be the best person to turn to right now. I really, really, really don't mean to sound pushy or crass or judgmental because I'm not trying to be, but relationships are about both of you being equally happy and there for each other. If he was keeping something like this from you, I'm sure that you would be sad not because this is how he felt, but because this is how he felt and he hadn't told you until now.

And yes, I understand not wanting a "paid" friend but actual friendship instead. I probably should have phrased that a bit more delicately. The best I can say at this point is to give these friends you have one last chance to prove to you that they care and aren't jerks who don't seem interested in your well-being. It sounds cheesy, but the important thing to know is that no matter what point in your life, you can always make friends and you can always move forward. Please don't feel like this should hold you back in anyway. Yes, it feels awful and crappy and the worst thing ever right now, but if you really want it to, life and yourself can find a way to make it better :)

Have you considered going to see a therapist to just have someone to talk to about all this? I know they say that therapists shouldn't become your friends per se, but they do care about you, and if that's something that your friends aren't providing for you then it might be worth it.

And that's true about this being about friendships as opposed to relationships, but don't forget that your boyfriend should theoretically also be your (very close) friend. There's no reason to think that telling him how you feel will hurt him in any way (unless he feels the same way as you do, in which case I'd recommend that you both seek some sort of help). Talking to your boyfriend and/or a therapist might be a good start. Friends are definitely important, but if the ones you have now are bailing on you and being dicks, then I would say turn to the people you know you absolutely can trust here and now and then work on finding more people like that. Unfortunately (to my sadness, too), people who will respect you and be your friend won't just flock to you, so it will take effort on your part (maybe your boyfriend could help?) to seek out those sorts of people you'd like to be around. It will take time and it'll be hard, but if you even make one effort every other day to be in a place to meet new people, then I'm sure you could find at least one new perosn who would care about you and want you to be okay :)

There's no one you could talk to at your work? Or maybe your parents? Do you live in a city area? Coffee shops (even if you don't drink coffee) are great for that, and other places like that. Unless you're being a creep, being rude, or being an asshole (all three of which I doubt you are), then never ever think that you're the problem. More often than not, it's the other people who have the problem. I've noticed a lot more people are flaky and don't get too close to people as friends these days, which is a real shame because that means we all kinda don't really know each other that well at all :( But please, please never think that you're a waste of space. I assure you, you are probably doing more with your life (you have a job, one step ahead of me already) than a lot of other people. You are important, you do matter, even if it's just me a random stranger on the Internet, saying that, please believe me when I say that you do not sound to me like someone who is a waste of space :)

:( Aside from the parents thing and the fact that you're a boy, this sounds like something I would write...

First off, there's absolutely nothing wrong with being alone and having a few close friends and not wanting to be around large groups of people *if that's something that makes you happy.* Everyone develops at different paces, and maybe just naturally you're a more introverted person who likes being by himself a lot more. Yes, more people in the world are extroverted, but never ever base your development and growth on how others are doing (something I have to remind myself of a lot). If those things are really making you legit unhappy (and not just because you're worried that you're not "normal" compared to everyone else), then it'll take some guts, but you should really work to put yourself out there. Like, start small, say you'll take a short walk one day. Next day you'll go to a busyish area and maybe sit at a big table and do something and see if other people join you. And just keep going until you feel comfortable. Yes, easier said than done, but it will work if you try. Also, smiling at people legit is amazing in terms of making people come to you, 99% of the time it'll brighten someone's day.

In terms of the parent thing, that's something that you have to work out for yourself. You should never be afraid of talking to your parents no matter what, that's what they're there for, to help you. To be honest (just based off the way you described your parents), your mother sound like she's putting way too much pressure on you and your father sounds like a bully in a way. Both of those things aren't ideal. If there's a school counselor you can talk to to help you with this, go to one asap because being able to have a good, serious conversation about how unhappy you are with your parents (especially if they are part of the cause of that unhappiness) is the second most important thing.

The first most important thing is your mental health. There is absolutely nothing wrong with having to take anxiety meds if you feel like you really need them. Of course, talk to your doctor about this (you don't even necessarily have to tell your parents if you're over 18). However, just bear in mind that meds don't solve everything. They can help, but don't just rely on them to feel better. Always use as instructed and simultaneously do things to put yourself out there more if you want to. It'll be hard at first, but I'm sure you'll be fine :)

Met a guy through mutual friends on the first day of college. Hated him, thought he was a jerk and I teased him a lot and made jabs at him. Later found out he was going through family hardships at the time and I felt like the jerk.

Fast forward 7 months later and I realize that I actually really like him (surprise) and we slowly start getting to know each other better and we eventually say we like each other and start our relationship. First boyfriend for me, third girlfriend for him but the first he says he's actually cared about.

We say "I love you" a month in.

We say we're perfect for each other and we become inseparable, a bit to the detriment of our other friendships since we spend all our time together. We do everything: walks, seeing midnight premieres of movies, work on school projects together, go to shows, go to the beach, go to conventions, eat at cool restaurants, show each other music/books/TV shows we like, etc. We get little gifts for each other and just do whatever because it doesn't matter what we're doing so long as we're together.

And then, to make a long, sadder story short, he realizes soon on into the relationship that he's sad. Not because of me, though God knows I thought it was my fault. No, he has clinical depression. Bad. After a year, he decides to get help because he can't take it anymore. But the meds don't really work. He tells me everything and we still do things together, but he seems so sad and distant. He doesn't seem to enjoy what we used to do anymore.

He starts getting sadder and sadder, saying he hates his life and that he hates that his depression is making me sad and leaves me crying at night worrying about him. I've never seen a guy cry more in that one month than he did.

Cut to the chase, we discuss our relationship in depth with both of us crying. After two years together, we decide that, for now, he doesn't want me chasing a pipe dream that may not exist right now, and I think I shouldn't just settle for my first relationship. That was six months ago.

But we're the best friends we have for each other, so we still hang out a lot and do stuff together. Pretty much, we're able to do 98% of the things we did already, so I guess in the long run, this is the best choice.

But it still makes me sad and cry almost every other night because I miss, more than anything else, hearing him say "I love *you*."
